stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance saw up to 90% speedup, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to higher quality model responses and faster inference times.
The updated engine also demonstrates reduced memory consumption when running models.

stories.author: unknown

stories.author: unknown

It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating the use of local LLMs.

bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed for local execution.
It integrates messaging applications with local AI coding agents.
The core feature emphasizes running all AI processes entirely on the user's own device for privacy/control.

bullet_points: Ollama introduces a new command for easily setting up and running coding tools.
It supports various models, including Claude Code, OpenCode, and Codex, locally or in the cloud.
A key feature is its simplicity, requiring no environment variables or configuration files.

stories.title: How AI could enable autonomous robot workers in workplaces—and maybe homes
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: The article discusses the evolution of robot autonomy, a key area in robotics research.
It explores the potential for AI to enable autonomous robot workers in both industrial and domestic settings.
Insights are provided by leading robotics researchers and founders regarding current technological advancements.

stories.title: From Fixed to Free Cameras: Calibration-Free View-Robust Vision-Language-Action Model
stories.author: Ran Xu
bullet_points: Addresses a critical real-world limitation in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models: fragility when camera setups change.
Proposes a novel approach where the VLA policy autonomously determines camera pose instead of relying on explicit extrinsic parameters.
Improves deployment robustness for robotics by making policies less dependent on fixed training-stage camera configurations.

stories.title: LLM-as-a-Verifier: A General-Purpose Verification Framework
stories.author: Azalia Mirhoseini
bullet_points: Introduces 'verification' as a new scaling axis for improving Large Language Model (LLM) capabilities, alongside compute scaling.
Presents 'LLM-as-a-Verifier,' a general-purpose framework designed to check the correctness of LLM outputs.
The framework offers fine-grained feedback for agentic tasks without necessitating additional model training.

stories.title: Search Beyond What Can Be Taught: Evolving the Knowledge Boundary in Agentic Visual Generation
stories.author: Cong Wei
bullet_points: Addresses the 'world-knowledge bottleneck' in visual generation models, where generators fabricate information outside their fixed training corpora.
Introduces SearchGen-20K and SearchGen-Bench, new benchmarks designed to test generative models against unbounded, long-tailed, and evolving user requests.
Focuses on enabling visual generation to 'search beyond what can be taught,' moving beyond mere rendering capabilities.

stories.title: From Fixed to Free Cameras: Calibration-Free View-Robust Vision-Language-Action Model
stories.author: Ran Xu
bullet_points: Addresses a critical real-world limitation in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models: fragility when camera setups change.
Proposes a novel approach where the model learns to be view-robust without requiring explicit camera extrinsic parameters.
This advancement significantly improves the practical deployability and robustness of AI agents in dynamic robotic environments.

stories.title: LLM-as-a-Verifier: A General-Purpose Verification Framework
stories.author: Azalia Mirhoseini
bullet_points: Introduces 'verification' as a new, crucial scaling axis for Large Language Models (LLMs), alongside compute scaling.
Presents 'LLM-as-a-Verifier,' a general-purpose framework designed to check the correctness of LLM outputs.
The framework offers fine-grained feedback for agentic tasks without necessitating additional model training.

stories.title: CompactionRL: Reinforcement Learning with Context Compaction for Long-Horizon Agents
stories.author: Yuxiao Dong
bullet_points: Addresses the critical limitation of finite context windows in long-horizon agentic LLMs.
Introduces CompactionRL, a novel reinforcement learning strategy for managing extended interaction trajectories.
Proposes using context compaction to summarize past states, allowing agents to operate beyond standard context limits.

stories.title: LLM-as-a-Verifier: A General-Purpose Verification Framework
stories.author: Azalia Mirhoseini
bullet_points: Introduces 'verification' as a new, critical scaling axis for Large Language Models (LLMs), alongside compute scaling.
Presents 'LLM-as-a-Verifier,' a general-purpose framework designed to assess the correctness of LLM outputs.
The framework offers fine-grained feedback for agentic tasks without necessitating additional model training.

stories.title: The best AI models cite retracted papers, and they cannot know it
stories.author: mikeeus
bullet_points: Frontier AI models are confidently citing retracted scientific papers from their training data.
The models demonstrate an inability to detect or flag these retractions, even for well-known ones.
The proposed solution requires external registry lookups, indicating a fundamental limitation in current model architectures.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings improved performance and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to enhance model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, particularly benefiting users on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The update also enables web search functionality within the Claude Code environment.
This suggests an enhancement in the complexity and capability of AI agent workflows.

stories.title: Solos debuts an even lighter version of its camera-less smart glasses
stories.author: Andrew Liszewski
bullet_points: Solos has released a new, significantly lighter version of its camera-less smart glasses, the AirGo A6.
The new model weighs approximately 19 grams, a substantial reduction from the previous 36-40 gram version.
Functionality relies on a voice-activated AI assistant, foregoing the use of cameras for a sleeker design.

stories.title: Google Search lets creators know more about their reach
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Google is enhancing Search Console to provide creators with better insights into their reach.
The new 'platform properties' feature allows users to track how search terms drive traffic to social media and YouTube content.
This update aims to give content owners clearer data on the discoverability of their profiles via Google Search.

stories.title: Kremlin suspected of flying drones over Europe using Russian shadow fleet
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Kremlin is suspected of using drones over Europe.
The drones may have been launched from Russian shadow fleet vessels.
The incident suggests Europe may lack adequate defenses against such intrusions.

stories.title: The incredible shrinking Xbox: Five studios, 3,200 employees let go
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Microsoft is undergoing significant restructuring within its gaming division.
The layoffs affect approximately 20% of the gaming workforce, including 3,200 employees across five studios.
The strategic shift involves refocusing the division's efforts on its most established and successful franchises.

stories.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization via Direct On-Policy Distillation
stories.author: Hao Zhou
bullet_points: Proposes a 'weak-to-strong' distillation method to improve large language models (LLMs) using Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR).
Addresses the computational bottleneck of traditional RLVR, which requires expensive rollouts on large, strong target models.
The method involves training RL on a smaller, cheaper model and then transferring that learned knowledge to enhance a larger target model.

stories.title: What Does a Discrete Diffusion Model Learn?
stories.author: Aran Raoufi
bullet_points: The paper investigates the fundamental learning mechanism of discrete diffusion models.
It rigorously derives the Continuous-Time Markov Chain (CTMC) Evidence Lower Bound (ELBO) for any noising process.
The core contribution is the 'Oracle Distance' theorem, linking the negative ELBO to the model's learned properties.

stories.title: Cortex: A Bidirectionally Aligned Embodied Agent Framework for Long-horizon Manipulation
stories.author: Tai Wang
bullet_points: Cortex is a new embodied agent framework designed to overcome the limitations of current Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models in long-horizon manipulation tasks.
It addresses the Markovian nature of existing models, which struggle with tasks requiring memory and long-term planning.
The framework features a 'bidirectionally aligned' design and a customized planning interface to bridge the gap between high-level planning and low-level execution.

stories.title: SPEARBench: A Benchmark for Naturalness Evaluation in Streaming Speech-to-Speech Language Models
stories.author: Laureano Moro-Velazquez
bullet_points: Introduces SPEARBench, a new benchmark specifically designed to evaluate the naturalness of streaming speech-to-speech language models.
Addresses a gap in current benchmarks by focusing on conversational aspects like timing, prosody, and turn-taking, rather than just standard speech/text metrics.
Aims to improve the perceived quality of conversational AI systems that respond directly with synthetic speech.

stories.title: REDDIT: Correcting Model-Generated Timestamp Drift in ASR without Forgetting via Replay-Based Distribution Editing
stories.author: Hung-yi Lee
bullet_points: Addresses a technical flaw in modern autoregressive ASR systems where generated timestamps drift over long non-speech segments.
Proposes a solution using 'Replay-Based Distribution Editing' to correct timestamp drift without degrading overall model performance.
Evaluates the issue across 15 different timestamp-producing ASR models using custom gap and long-gap benchmarks.

stories.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization via Direct On-Policy Distillation
stories.author: Hao Zhou
bullet_points: Addresses the computational bottleneck of Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) when scaling large language models.
Proposes a 'weak-to-strong' distillation method: training RL on a smaller, cheaper model first.
The learned knowledge from the smaller model is then reused to improve a larger, stronger target model.

stories.title: Interpretable Human-Label-Free Deep Learning for Real-Bogus Classification with Uncertainty Quantification
stories.author: Vincenzo Piuri
bullet_points: Addresses the critical problem of Real-Bogus classification in automated transient discovery pipelines.
Proposes a novel deep learning framework capable of training without expensive human-labeled data.
Focuses on robustness against class contamination and provides calibrated uncertainty quantification.

stories.title: TabPack: Efficient Hyperparameter Ensembles for Tabular Deep Learning
stories.author: Artem Babenko
bullet_points: Introduces TabPack, a new efficient ensemble method for deep learning on tabular data.
Addresses the inefficiency of existing MLP ensembles which rely on uniform hyperparameters.
Claims strong out-of-the-box performance, reducing the need for extensive hyperparameter tuning.

stories.title: Faithfulness to Refusal: A Causal Audit of Neuron Selectors
stories.author: Vinay Kumar Sankarapu
bullet_points: The paper addresses the gap between attribution scores (which identify important neurons) and true causal importance in language models.
It introduces paired audits using one-shot neuron-row zeroing to causally test the effectiveness of neuron selectors.
Findings show that attribution methods significantly outperform simpler baselines in identifying dispensable neuron rows.

stories.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization via Direct On-Policy Distillation
stories.author: Hao Zhou
bullet_points: Addresses the computational bottleneck of Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) when training large language models.
Proposes a 'weak-to-strong' distillation method: train RL on a smaller, cheaper model first.
Reuses the learned knowledge from the smaller model to improve a larger, stronger target model, reducing training costs.

stories.title: SPEARBench: A Benchmark for Naturalness Evaluation in Streaming Speech-to-Speech Language Models
stories.author: Laureano Moro-Velazquez
bullet_points: Introduces SPEARBench, a new benchmark specifically designed for evaluating the naturalness of streaming speech-to-speech language models.
Addresses a gap in current benchmarks by focusing on conversational quality factors beyond standard metrics, such as timing, prosody, and turn-taking.
Aims to improve the perceived quality of systems that directly respond to spoken queries with synthetic speech.

stories.title: REDDIT: Correcting Model-Generated Timestamp Drift in ASR without Forgetting via Replay-Based Distribution Editing
stories.author: Hung-yi Lee
bullet_points: Addresses a critical issue in modern ASR systems where generated timestamps can drift over long non-speech segments.
Proposes a novel solution using Replay-Based Distribution Editing to correct timestamp drift without degrading transcription quality.
Evaluates the method across 15 different timestamp-producing ASR systems using custom gap and long-gap benchmarks.

stories.title: Faithfulness to Refusal: A Causal Audit of Neuron Selectors
stories.author: Vinay Kumar Sankarapu
bullet_points: The research addresses the gap between attribution scores (identifying important neurons) and actual causal importance in large language models.
The study employs paired audits using one-shot neuron-row zeroing to test causal significance.
Attribution methods are shown to significantly outperform simpler baselines in identifying dispensable neuron rows for model pruning and interpretability.

stories.title: Selective Disclosure Watermarking for Large Language Models
stories.author: Qi Long
bullet_points: The research addresses a limitation in current LLM watermarking: the inability to selectively disclose embedded signals.
Existing watermarking methods (zero-bit and multi-bit) are used to distinguish synthetic LLM text or embed metadata.
The proposed 'Selective Disclosure Watermarking' aims to allow verification of specific parts of the watermark without revealing the entire message.

stories.title: How Much is Left? LLMs Linearly Encode Their Remaining Output Length
stories.author: Adam Oberman
bullet_points: The research investigates whether LLMs possess an internal estimate of their remaining output length, given their token-by-token generation process.
Using linear probes on frozen hidden states of 7-8B open-weight models, the study analyzes predictable length structures in various response types (solutions, retrievals, retractions).
The findings suggest that LLMs exhibit remarkably consistent and measurable length patterns in their generated outputs.

stories.title: AI Wrote a Thread-Safe Counter. The CPU Made It 5x Slower.
stories.author: mrviduus
bullet_points: The article explores the performance implications of AI-generated code for a simple concurrency problem (thread-safe counter).
It introduces the concept of the cache line and how hardware architecture impacts software performance.
The core finding is that the CPU overhead significantly slowed down the AI-generated solution.

stories.title: Observability Design for the AI Era — Application / Infrastructure / CI / LLM, Each in Its Own Shape (Part 1)
stories.author: ryantsuji
bullet_points: The article discusses the need to reshape observability practices to accommodate the demands of the AI era.
It analyzes four distinct axes of observability: application, infrastructure, CI, and LLM, noting their unique design requirements.
Key design decisions highlighted include client-side Gemini cost computation and routing specific LLM telemetry (e.g., Claude Code OTel) to BigQuery.

stories.title: Self-Hosting a Model Means Self-Hosting Its Evaluation Too
stories.author: aiexplore369zoho
bullet_points: Self-hosting AI models shifts the operational burden to the user.
The responsibility for model evaluation is transferred from vendors to the end-user.
This trend implies users must manage the entire lifecycle of local AI, including monitoring and testing.
